title: Dimension at a point of a finite type algebra is preserved by extension of the ground field
statement: Let $k$ and $K$ be fields, $\iota:k\to K$ a ring homomorphism, $S$ a finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $S_K=S\otimes_kK$, a $K$-algebra through $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$, with the ring map $j:S\to S_K$, $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Let $\mathfrak q_K\subset S_K$ be a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$, a prime ideal of $S$. Then the Krull dimensions of the topological spaces $\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}S_K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the points $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q_K$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] are equal: $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim_{\mathfrak q_K}(\operatorname{Spec}S_K)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, line 28307), with S_K = K (x)_k S there; this node writes S (x)_k K, isomorphic by the swap

proof.text: (Presentations and primes.) By [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] there are $n\ge0$ and a surjective $k$-algebra homomorphism $\alpha:P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; let $I=\ker\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] $P$ is Noetherian, so $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ for some $f_1,\dots,f_m\in P$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $P_K=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $\kappa:P\to P_K$ the ring map applying $\iota$ to the coefficients. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] (with $R=k$, $R'=K$, $A=S$, $\pi=\alpha$) the $K$-algebra map $\alpha':P_K\to S_K$, $x_i\mapsto\alpha(x_i)\otimes1$, is surjective with kernel $I'=(\kappa(f_1),\dots,\kappa(f_m))$. The ring maps $\alpha'\circ\kappa$ and $j\circ\alpha:P\to S_K$ agree on the constants ($c\mapsto1\otimes\iota(c)=\iota(c)\cdot(1\otimes1)$) and on every $x_i$, hence are equal [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $\mathfrak q'=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, a prime of $P$ containing $I$, and $\mathfrak q'_K=\alpha'^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)$, a prime of $P_K$ containing $I'$. Then $\kappa^{-1}(\mathfrak q'_K)=(\alpha'\circ\kappa)^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)=(j\circ\alpha)^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K)=\alpha^{-1}(j^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K))=\alpha^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak q'$, so $\mathfrak q'_K$ lies over $\mathfrak q'$ just as $\mathfrak q_K$ lies over $\mathfrak q$: this is the commutative square of the source, with vertical maps $\kappa$ and $j$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, proof from line 28319), 'Choose a presentation S = k[x_1,...,x_n]/I. This gives a presentation K (x)_k S = K[x_1,...,x_n]/(K (x)_k I). Let q_K', resp. q' be the corresponding primes'

proof.text: (The four rings are Noetherian and both vertical maps are flat.) $P$ and $P_K$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring] (over $k$, resp. $K$); $S\cong P/I$ and $S_K\cong P_K/I'$ (step 1) are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (with $R=P$, resp. $R=P_K$, and $n=0$). Since $\iota:k\to K$ is a ring homomorphism of fields, $K/k$ is a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] (with $D=S$) the map $j:S\to S\otimes_kK=S_K$ is faithfully flat, hence flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map]. Likewise (with $D=P$) $\epsilon:P\to P\otimes_kK$, $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, is flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change] applied to $A=P$, $\pi=\mathrm{id}_P$, $m=0$, the $K$-algebra map $\pi':P_K\to P\otimes_kK$, $x_i\mapsto x_i\otimes1$, is bijective, and $\pi'\circ\kappa=\epsilon$ (both ring maps send $c\in k$ to $1\otimes\iota(c)=c\otimes1$ and $x_i$ to $x_i\otimes1$). So $\kappa=\pi'^{-1}\circ\epsilon$ makes $P_K$ a $P$-module isomorphic to $P\otimes_kK$ through $\pi'$, and $\kappa$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] (the flatness condition is invariant under an isomorphism of $P$-modules). (The source localizes these flat maps at the primes; the height formula of step 4 is stated for the global flat maps and the primes, so no localization is needed here.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, proof from line 28319), 'Both vertical arrows are flat because they are localizations of the flat ring maps S -> S_K and k[x_1,...,x_n] -> K[x_1,...,x_n]'

proof.text: (The vertical maps have the same fibre rings.) Let $\mathfrak q'P_K$ be the ideal of $P_K$ generated by $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ and $\mathfrak qS_K$ the ideal of $S_K$ generated by $j(\mathfrak q)$. Since $\alpha$ is surjective, $\alpha(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak q$, so $\alpha'(\mathfrak q'P_K)$, the ideal generated by $\alpha'(\kappa(\mathfrak q'))=j(\alpha(\mathfrak q'))=j(\mathfrak q)$ ($\alpha'$ surjective, so the image of an ideal is an ideal and the image of the ideal generated by a set is the ideal generated by its image), equals $\mathfrak qS_K$. Also $\ker\alpha'=I'\subseteq\mathfrak q'P_K$, as $I'$ is generated by the $\kappa(f_j)$ with $f_j\in I\subseteq\mathfrak q'$. Hence $\alpha'^{-1}(\mathfrak qS_K)=\mathfrak q'P_K+\ker\alpha'=\mathfrak q'P_K$, and $\alpha'$ induces a ring isomorphism $\bar\alpha':P_K/\mathfrak q'P_K\to S_K/\mathfrak qS_K$. Moreover $\mathfrak q'P_K\subseteq\mathfrak q'_K$ (as $\kappa(\mathfrak q')\subseteq\mathfrak q'_K$ by step 1) and $\mathfrak qS_K\subseteq\mathfrak q_K$ (as $j(\mathfrak q)\subseteq\mathfrak q_K$), and $\bar\alpha'$ maps the prime $\mathfrak q'_K/\mathfrak q'P_K$ onto $\alpha'(\mathfrak q'_K)/\mathfrak qS_K=\mathfrak q_K/\mathfrak qS_K$ ($\alpha'(\alpha'^{-1}(\mathfrak q_K))=\mathfrak q_K$ by surjectivity). A ring isomorphism carries chains of primes contained in a prime bijectively to chains contained in its image, so $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q'_K/\mathfrak q'P_K)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q_K/\mathfrak qS_K)=:h$, heights computed in $P_K/\mathfrak q'P_K$ and $S_K/\mathfrak qS_K$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, proof from line 28319), 'Moreover, the vertical arrows have the same fibre rings'

proof.text: (Heights.) By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference] (over $k$ with $S=P/I$ via $\alpha$, and over $K$ with $S_K=P_K/I'$ via $\alpha'$) the heights $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q\le\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'\le n$ and $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q_K\le\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'_K\le n$ are finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-height-formula], applied to the flat map $\kappa:P\to P_K$ of Noetherian rings with the prime $\mathfrak q'_K$ over $\mathfrak q'$ and to the flat map $j:S\to S_K$ of Noetherian rings with the prime $\mathfrak q_K$ over $\mathfrak q$ (steps 1 and 2), $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'_K=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q'_K/\mathfrak q'P_K)$ and $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q_K=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q_K/\mathfrak qS_K)$. Both fibre terms equal $h$ (step 3), and $h\le\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'_K\le n$ is finite, so subtracting: $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'-\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'_K-\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q_K$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, proof from line 28319), 'Hence, we see from Lemma 00ON (lemma-dimension-base-fibre-equals-total) that height(q') - height(q) = height(q_K') - height(q_K)'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The isomorphism $P/I\cong S$ induced by $\alpha$ gives a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}(P/I)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] sending $\mathfrak q$ to $\mathfrak q'/I$, and the dimension at a point [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] is preserved by homeomorphisms (open neighbourhoods and their Krull dimensions correspond); likewise for $\alpha'$, $S_K$, $\mathfrak q_K$ and $\mathfrak q'_K/I'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference] over $k$ and over $K$, $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-(\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'-\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q)$ and $\dim_{\mathfrak q_K}(\operatorname{Spec}S_K)=n-(\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q'_K-\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q_K)$. By step 4 the right-hand sides are equal, so $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=\dim_{\mathfrak q_K}(\operatorname{Spec}S_K)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00P4 (label lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension, proof from line 28319), the displayed chain n - dim_x X = dim_{x'} X' - dim_x X = height(q') - height(q) = height(q_K') - height(q_K) = dim_{x'_K} X'_K - dim_{x_K} X_K = n - dim_{x_K} X_K, by Lemma 00P2 (lemma-codimension) with dim_{x'} X' = n
